title: Tesla now has more than 300 robotaxis in Austin after Cybercab launch
key_facts: Tesla says it now has more than 300 self-driving taxis serving Austin.
The Robotaxi Tracker counts 354 Tesla robotaxis on the street in Austin, including 178 gold Cybercabs.
The Cybercab, with no steering wheel or pedals, debuted in Austin on 3 Sep.
Waymo also has more than 300 robotaxis in Austin, about 700 autonomous vehicles in total.

The US Department of Transportation recently opened an investigation after reports that some of the cars sped through school zones, according to Peter Kurdock of Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety.
NHTSA announced a Cybercab investigation the day after the launch and says it is developing safety rules; no federal standards cover self-driving software, Kurdock said.
quote_evidence: Tesla says it now has more than 300 self-driving taxis serving Austin.
According to the Robotaxi Tracker, Tesla’s fleet has 354 robotaxis on the street in Austin, including 178 gold-colored Cybercabs.
Kurdock said, “There are no federal safety standards that apply to the software in these cars that are driving themselves, and that’s a real concern.”
why_it_matters_hint: Robotaxis are becoming common in Austin, while safety regulators and advocates question the pace.
event_date: Cybercab launch 3 Sep 2026; fleet figures reported 14-15 Oct 2026
notes: Fleet figures come from Tesla and a third-party tracker.
